french: Je demande toujours à Darcy un thé à base de plantes relaxantes... Il me faut une bonne nuit de sommeil pour être en forme le lendemain !
russian: Я всегда прошу у Дарси чай с её самыми успокаивающими травами... Важно хорошенько высыпаться, чтобы следующий день прошёл на ура!
bulgarian: I always ask Darcy for a tea with her most relaxing herbs... I need a full night's sleep so I can make the most of the next day!

english: Louis gave me a hard time when I cut the sleeves off one of his shirts, but it gets hot working in a field in the dead of summer!
french: Louis m'en a fait voir quand j'ai coupé les manches d'une de ses chemises, mais ça donne chaud de travailler aux champs en plein été !
russian: Луи ругался, когда я отрезал рукава у его рубашки... но в поле летом — жарко!
bulgarian: Louis gave me a hard time when I cut the sleeves off one of his shirts, but it gets hot working in a field in the dead of summer!

english: I'm not an expert on whether they look nice, but they stand up to a lot when I'm out working the farm.
french: N'étant pas spécialiste, je ne sais pas s'ils sont beaux, mais ils résistent à beaucoup de choses, quand je bosse sur la ferme.
russian: Не знаю уж, как они на мне выглядят, но работу на ферме они выдерживают что надо.
bulgarian: I'm not an expert on whether they look nice, but they stand up to a lot when I'm out working the farm.

english: I think Louis has some of those reinforced pants back in stock...
french: Je crois que Louis a encore en stock quelques-uns de ses pantalons renforcés...
russian: Кажется, у Луи снова в продаже укреплённые штаны...
bulgarian: I think Louis has some of those reinforced pants back in stock...

english: I usually wear my shirts out before getting a new one... Louis always intervenes before it gets too bad.
french: J'use en général mes chemises jusqu'à la corde avant d'en racheter... Louis intervient toujours avant que ça se gâte trop.
russian: Я обычно изнашиваю рубашки до дыр, прежде чем покупать новые... Но Луи всегда вмешивается прежде, чем дойдёт до крайностей.
bulgarian: I usually wear my shirts out before getting a new one... Louis always intervenes before it gets too bad.

english: Louis once spent an hour talking me into a sun hat. I bring it everywhere in the summer!
french: Une fois, Louis a passé une heure à me convaincre d'acheter un chapeau de paille. En été, je ne le quitte jamais !
russian: Луи однажды целый час уговаривал меня носить шляпу от солнца. Теперь я с ней летом не расстаюсь!
bulgarian: Louis once spent an hour talking me into a sun hat. I bring it everywhere in the summer!

english: [Ari], are you browsing Merri's shop? Most of my furniture back on the farm is restored by her.
french: [Ari], tu regardes ce que Merri a en boutique ? C'est elle qui a restauré la plupart de mes meubles, à la ferme.
russian: [Ari], как тебе у Мэрри в лавке? У меня почти вся мебель на ферме — её работы.
bulgarian: [Ari], are you browsing Merri's shop? Most of my furniture back on the farm is restored by her.

english: I like any kind of furniture that looks sturdy... see, I like to do a lot of leaning, and there's been accidents...
french: J'aime tous les meubles qui ont l'air costaud... J'aime bien m'appuyer dessus, tu vois, et... il y a eu quelques accidents...
russian: Мне нравится крепкая мебель... я люблю облокачиваться, а это... иногда приводит к бедам.
bulgarian: I like any kind of furniture that looks sturdy... see, I like to do a lot of leaning, and there's been accidents...

english: Olric and I take turns giving Merri a hand on Market days... she's got a lot of heavy furniture, takes some muscle to arrange it all.
french: Avec Olric, on se relaie pour donner un coup de main à Merri les jours de marché... Elle a plein de meubles lourds, il faut un peu de muscle pour tout mettre en place.
russian: Мы с Ольриком помогаем Мэрри на базаре по очереди... у неё мебель тяжёлая, так что нужно мускулы.
bulgarian: Olric and I take turns giving Merri a hand on Market days... she's got a lot of heavy furniture, takes some muscle to arrange it all.

english: Want to hear a secret, [Ari]? Merri's got muscle... I saw her moving a wardrobe around like it was nothing!
french: Tu veux que je te dise un secret, [Ari] ? Merri est musclée... Je l'ai vue une fois déplacer une penderie comme si de rien n'était !
russian: Хочешь секрет, [Ari]? У Мэрри силушка что надо... сам видел, как она шкаф тащила, будто это пушинка!
bulgarian: Want to hear a secret, [Ari]? Merri's got muscle... I saw her moving a wardrobe around like it was nothing!

english: When I asked her about it, she said she didn't mention it because she likes when Olric and I help out.
french: Quand je l'ai interrogée, elle m'a répondu qu'elle n'avait rien dit parce qu'elle aime bien qu'on lui donne un coup de main, avec Olric.
russian: Когда я спросил её об этом, она сказала, что не хотела говорить, потому что ей нравится, когда мы с Ольриком помогаем.
bulgarian: When I asked her about it, she said she didn't mention it because she likes when Olric and I help out.

english: Stillwell said I would live under a shroud of darkness for my transgressions... what am I going to do, [Ari]?! My crops won't grow under a shroud!
bulgarian: Stillwell said I would live under a shroud of darkness for my transgressions... what am I going to do, [Ari]?! My crops won't grow under a shroud!

english: Stillwell says "the creaky wheel of fate turns, withering the old to welcome the new". That sounds bad, right [Ari]?! It's bad!
bulgarian: Stillwell says "the creaky wheel of fate turns, withering the old to welcome the new". That sounds bad, right [Ari]?! It's bad!

english: Valen says I should stop getting fortunes from Stillwell because it raises my blood pressure... which is a lot like what Stillwell told me when he said "THE BLOOD, IT RISES"!
bulgarian: Valen says I should stop getting fortunes from Stillwell because it raises my blood pressure... which is a lot like what Stillwell told me when he said "THE BLOOD, IT RISES"!

english: Stillwell told me "Today, we will be like the dead"! And then he fainted! And then I fainted! IT CAME TRUE, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Stillwell told me "Today, we will be like the dead"! And then he fainted! And then I fainted! IT CAME TRUE, [Ari]!

english: For starters, the dishes he makes are tiny!
french: Pour commencer, ses plats sont minuscules !
russian: Начнём с того, что у него крошечные блюда!
bulgarian: For starters, the dishes he makes are tiny!

english: Who are you feeding with portions like that? An ant?
french: Qui peut survivre avec de si petites portions ? Des fourmis ?
russian: Кого ты хочешь накормить такими порциями? Муравья?
bulgarian: Who are you feeding with portions like that? An ant?

english: Between you and me, I just don't know if I agree with Taliferro's cooking philosophies.
french: Entre nous, je ne suis pas sûr d'apprécier la conception que Taliferro a de la cuisine.
russian: Между нами говоря, я не уверен, что готов согласиться с подходом Талиферро к готовке.
bulgarian: Between you and me, I just don't know if I agree with Taliferro's cooking philosophies.

english: You have to eat enough to work the field, and you want plenty of extra in case the neighbors come over!
french: Quand on travaille dans les champs, il faut manger à sa faim et prévoir un peu plus pour les voisins de passage !
russian: Надо есть достаточно, чтобы работать в поле, а ещё запас на случай, если придут соседи!
bulgarian: You have to eat enough to work the field, and you want plenty of extra in case the neighbors come over!

english: Maybe he doesn't have any neighbors? With a personality like that, I'd believe it...
french: Ou alors, il n'apprécie pas ses voisins ? Vu son caractère, ce ne serait pas très étonnant...
russian: Может, у него нет соседей? С его характером, поверить нетрудно...
bulgarian: Maybe he doesn't have any neighbors? With a personality like that, I'd believe it...

english: Meals gotta be big, [Ari]. You'd think a fancy chef like Taliferro would understand that!
french: Un repas doit être copieux, [Ari]. Un chef renommé comme Taliferro devrait le savoir !
russian: Блюда должны быть большими, [Ari]. Казалось бы, модный шеф вроде Талиферро должен понимать!
bulgarian: Meals gotta be big, [Ari]. You'd think a fancy chef like Taliferro would understand that!

english: She would out-haughty him in two flaps of her left wing!
french: En deux coups d'aile, elle lui ferait comprendre qui est la plus présomptueuse.
russian: Она его переспесит одним левым крылом!
bulgarian: She would out-haughty him in two flaps of her left wing!

english: Taliferro is the haughty type, but he's got nothing on Henrietta.
french: Taliferro est du genre présomptueux, mais il n'arrive pas à la patte d'Henrietta.
russian: Талиферро, конечно, спесивый тип, но с Генриеттой не сравнить.
bulgarian: Taliferro is the haughty type, but he's got nothing on Henrietta.

english: But I think he misses one thing. Food should make you happy!
french: Mais il passe à côté de l'essentiel. Pour moi, la nourriture doit nous rendre heureux !
russian: Но, по-моему, он упускает главное. Еда должна приносить радость!
bulgarian: But I think he misses one thing. Food should make you happy!

english: He seems miserable to me!
french: Il a l'air tellement triste.
russian: А он выглядит так несчастно!
bulgarian: He seems miserable to me!

english: I'll admit, Taliferro knows a lot about cooking. He's an expert.
french: C'est vrai, Taliferro s'y connaît en cuisine. C'est un expert.
russian: Готов признать, Талиферро разбирается в готовке. Он эксперт.
bulgarian: I'll admit, Taliferro knows a lot about cooking. He's an expert.

english: I thought about dyeing my hair, but what if my animals didn't recognize me after? That would downright break my heart.
french: J'ai déjà pensé à me teindre les cheveux, mais si jamais mes animaux ne me reconnaissaient plus, après ? Ça me briserait le cœur.
russian: Я думал покрасить волосы, но вдруг животные меня не узнают? Я этого не переживу.
bulgarian: I thought about dyeing my hair, but what if my animals didn't recognize me after? That would downright break my heart.

english: I should probably let Vera take some shears to this mane of mine more often... I do let it get a little wild.
french: Je devrais sûrement laisser Vera me rafraîchir la crinière un peu plus souvent... J'ai tendance à avoir une sacrée tignasse.
russian: Надо бы почаще давать Вере подстричь эту мою гриву... уж больно буйная.
bulgarian: I should probably let Vera take some shears to this mane of mine more often... I do let it get a little wild.

english: Vera always compliments my hair... in fact, she talked me out of cutting it short.
french: Vera me fait souvent des compliments sur mes cheveux... D'ailleurs, elle m'a déconseillé de me les couper court.
russian: Вера всегда хвалит мои волосы... даже отговорила коротко стричь.
bulgarian: Vera always compliments my hair... in fact, she talked me out of cutting it short.

english: I don't think I'd dye my hair green, but I wonder if Henrietta would get a kick out of green feathers... what do you think, [Ari]?
french: Je n'irais pas me teindre les cheveux en vert, mais je me demande si ça plairait à Henrietta d'avoir des plumes vertes... Qu'est-ce que tu en penses, [Ari] ?
russian: Я бы зелёный себе не сделал, но Генриетте, может, понравились бы зелёные перья... как думаешь, [Ari]?
bulgarian: I don't think I'd dye my hair green, but I wonder if Henrietta would get a kick out of green feathers... what do you think, [Ari]?

english: But to be honest I'm not sure how useful it'd be down on the farm.
french: Honnêtement, je ne vois pas trop à quoi ça me servirait à la ferme.
russian: Но, честно говоря, я не уверен, насколько оно нужно на ферме.
bulgarian: But to be honest I'm not sure how useful it'd be down on the farm.

english: Wheedle tried to talk me into buying some of that $Snake Oil$ of his...
french: Wheedle a essayé de me vendre un peu de son $huile de couleuvre$...
russian: Хлюст пытался уговорить меня купить его $змеиное масло$...
bulgarian: Wheedle tried to talk me into buying some of that $Snake Oil$ of his...

english: I think he's exaggerating, though. She'll get big as a cow at most, I bet.
french: Il exagère encore. Au mieux, elle fera la taille d'une vache.
russian: Но я думаю, он преувеличивает. Наверняка вырастет не больше коровы.
bulgarian: I think he's exaggerating, though. She'll get big as a cow at most, I bet.

english: Wheedle sold me a bag of something he called Giganto Feed... he says it'll make Henrietta as big as a house!
french: Wheedle m'a vendu un sachet de « graines Gigantis »... D'après lui, Henrietta deviendra grande comme une maison si elle en mange !
russian: Хлюст продал мне мешок смеси, которую он называет гиганто-корм... Говорит, что с ним Генриетта будет размером с дом!
bulgarian: Wheedle sold me a bag of something he called Giganto Feed... he says it'll make Henrietta as big as a house!

english: And he says it's a healthy and nutritionally dense superfood, to boot! Wait till I tell Valen about this!
french: En plus, il dit que c'est un super aliment très sain et très équilibré sur le plan nutritionnel ! Quand je dirai ça à Valen !
russian: К тому же, по его словам, это здоровая и крайне питательная суперпища! Вот Вален обрадуется, когда я ей расскажу!
bulgarian: And he says it's a healthy and nutritionally dense superfood, to boot! Wait till I tell Valen about this!

english: Have you tried that $Fast Food$ at Wheedle's store? It's so good, I can't stop eating it!
french: As-tu goûté l'$encas sur le pouce$ de Wheedle ? J'adore, je ne peux plus m'en passer !
russian:
Ты

пробовали

пробовалапробовалпробовало $фастфуд$ в лавке Хлюста? Он такой вкусный, что я не могу оторваться!
bulgarian: Have you tried that $Fast Food$ at Wheedle's store? It's so good, I can't stop eating it!

english: They can put all kinds of things into globes these days!
french: On peut mettre tout un tas de choses dans une boule de nos jours !
russian: Чего только не кладут нынче в шарики!
bulgarian: They can put all kinds of things into globes these days!

english: That $Snow Globe$ at Wheedle's booth is really something!
french: La $boule à neige$ du stand de Wheedle est incroyable !
russian: Какой интересный у Хлюста $снежный шар$ в лавке!
bulgarian: That $Snow Globe$ at Wheedle's booth is really something!

english: We'll see! Henrietta's got sophisticated tastes.
french: On verra bien ! Henrietta a des goûts très éclectiques.
russian: Вот увидим! У Генриетты весьма придирчивый вкус!
bulgarian: We'll see! Henrietta's got sophisticated tastes.

english: Gya ha ha!
french: Gah ha ha !
russian: Га-ха-ха!
bulgarian: Gya ha ha!

english: Zorel sold me a $Song Crystal$ that she says my animals will love.
french: Zorel m'a vendu un $cristal musical$, elle dit que mes animaux vont l'adorer.
russian: Зорель продала мне один $поющий кристалл$. Сказала, моим животным точно понравится.
bulgarian: Zorel sold me a $Song Crystal$ that she says my animals will love.

english: Keep it up, little guy!
french: Continue comme ça, petit gars !
russian: Так держать, кроха!
bulgarian: Keep it up, little guy!

english: I saw that $Deep Earthworm$ at the Museum. I've got admiration for any creature that works the soil.
french: J'ai vu ce $ver des profondeurs$ au musée. J'admire toutes les créatures qui travaillent la terre.
russian: Видел в музее $глубинного червяка$. Уважаю любое создание, что рыхлит почву.
bulgarian: I saw that $Deep Earthworm$ at the Museum. I've got admiration for any creature that works the soil.

english: What an impeccable weaving technique! I'm inspired to try it myself.
french: Quelle technique de tressage impeccable ! Ça me donne envie d'essayer.
russian: Какое безупречное плетение! Я даже сам захотел попробовать.
bulgarian: What an impeccable weaving technique! I'm inspired to try it myself.

english: Were you the one who donated the $Gathering Basket$ to the Museum, [Ari]?
french: C'est toi qui as fait don du $panier de cueillette$ au musée, [Ari] ?
russian:
Это ты

пожертвовали

пожертвовалапожертвовалпожертвовало $плетёную корзину$ музею, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Were you the one who donated the $Gathering Basket$ to the Museum, [Ari]?

english: That camouflage is the real deal!
french: Son camouflage, c'est quelque chose !
russian: У него отменный камуфляж!
bulgarian: That camouflage is the real deal!

english: You know, I'm still not sure if I managed to spy that $Hidden Beetle$ at the Museum.
french: Tu sais, je ne suis même pas certain d'avoir réussi à observer le $scarabée furtif$, au musée.
russian: Знаешь, я до сих пор не понял, удалось ли мне найти в музее $скрытного жука$.
bulgarian: You know, I'm still not sure if I managed to spy that $Hidden Beetle$ at the Museum.

english: So they're already roasted when you pick them up.
french: Elles sont donc déjà grillées quand on les ramasse.
russian: И что они уже поджаренные, когда их собираешь.
bulgarian: So they're already roasted when you pick them up.

english: Talk about convenience!
french: Si c'est pas pratique, ça !
russian: Вот это удобно!
bulgarian: Talk about convenience!

english: Errol was telling me that those $Lava Chestnuts$ you donated to the Museum grow near magma...
french: Errol me racontait que les $châtaignes de lave$ dont tu as fait don au musée poussent près du magma...
russian:
Эррол мне сказал, что эти $лавовые каштаны$, которые ты

отдали

отдалаотдалотдало в музей, растут возле магмы...
bulgarian: Errol was telling me that those $Lava Chestnuts$ you donated to the Museum grow near magma...

english: Never knew what that meant until I saw that Muskie at the Museum.
french: Je n'avais jamais compris ce que ça voulait dire avant de voir ce maskinongé, au musée.
russian: Я плохо представлял, о чём она, пока не увидел эту рыбу в музее.
bulgarian: Never knew what that meant until I saw that Muskie at the Museum.

english: They're whoppers! Way to go, Grandma!
french: Ils sont énormes ! Chapeau, mamie !
russian: Они же гигантские! Ну ты даёшь, бабуля!
bulgarian: They're whoppers! Way to go, Grandma!

english: Grandma once told me she caught two $Muskies$ with her bare hands, one under each arm.
french: Ma grand-mère m'a raconté un jour qu'elle avait attrapé deux $maskinongés$ à mains nues, un sous chaque bras.
russian: Бабушка мне однажды рассказывала, как голыми руками поймала двух $маскинонгов$. Одного в одну руку, другого во вторую.
bulgarian: Grandma once told me she caught two $Muskies$ with her bare hands, one under each arm.

english: Reminds me of that old legend about a horse that could turn into a fish!
french: Il me fait penser à cette vieille légende à propos d'un cheval capable de se transformer en poisson !
russian: Я на него посмотрел и сразу вспомнил легенду про лошадь, которая преварщалась в рыбу!
bulgarian: Reminds me of that old legend about a horse that could turn into a fish!

english: That seems unlikely.
french: Ça semble improbable.
russian: Хотя это было бы маловероятно.
bulgarian: That seems unlikely.

english: You know that $Silver Redhorse$ you donated to the Museum?
french: Tu sais, ce $chevalier blanc$ dont tu as fait don au musée ?
russian:
Помнишь $серебряного чукучана$, которого ты

отдали

отдалаотдалотдало в музей?
bulgarian: You know that $Silver Redhorse$ you donated to the Museum?

english: I was trying to figure the breed, but it's awfully hard to concentrate when I'm looking at that round little face. Can't get enough of it!
french: J'ai essayé d'identifier de quelle espèce il est, mais j'ai bien du mal à me concentrer quand je regarde sa petite tête ronde. Je ne m'en lasse pas !
russian: Я пытался угадать породу, но как тут сосредоточиться, когда смотришь в эти круглые щёчки? Не могу налюбоваться!
bulgarian: I was trying to figure the breed, but it's awfully hard to concentrate when I'm looking at that round little face. Can't get enough of it!

english: That =Stone Horse= in the Museum's collection is so cute, [Ari].
french: Le =cheval de pierre= des collections du musée est vraiment joli, [Ari].
russian: Эта =каменная лошадка= в музейной коллекции такая умилительная, [Ari].
bulgarian: That =Stone Horse= in the Museum's collection is so cute, [Ari].

english: It sure is cute. But the smell...
french: Il est mignon, c'est sûr. Mais alors, son odeur...
russian: На вид ужасно милый. А вот запах...
bulgarian: It sure is cute. But the smell...

english: Not so much.
french: Beaucoup moins.
russian: Это совсем другое.
bulgarian: Not so much.

english: I saw it! That $Sulfur Crab$ at the Museum!
french: Je l'ai vu ! Ce $crabe sulfuré$, au musée !
russian: Я видел в музее этого $серного краба$!
bulgarian: I saw it! That $Sulfur Crab$ at the Museum!

english: Usually I can identify the animal hair that went into making a brush, but that one? I just don't know!
french: D'habitude, j'arrive à identifier quel poil d'animal a été utilisé pour fabriquer une brosse, mais celle-ci ? Impossible à dire !
russian: Обычно я могу определить, из чьей шерсти сделана щётка, но эта... Без понятия!
bulgarian: Usually I can identify the animal hair that went into making a brush, but that one? I just don't know!

english: The $Vintage Brush$ at the Museum is mysterious.
french: La $brosse rétro$, au musée, est très mystérieuse.
russian: $Старинная щётка$ в музее — настоящая загадка.
bulgarian: The $Vintage Brush$ at the Museum is mysterious.

english: You don't suppose it's hers...?
french: Tu ne crois quand même pas que c'est la sienne...?
russian: Ты ведь не думаешь, что это он?..
bulgarian: You don't suppose it's hers...?

english: That $Vintage Cow Bell$ at the Museum really took me back! Grandma had one just like it!
french: La $cloche de vache rétro$, au musée, a fait remonter chez moi de très vieux souvenirs ! Ma grand-mère en avait une comme ça !
russian: $Старинный коровий колокольчик$ в музее прям вернул меня в детство! У бабушки был точно такой же!
bulgarian: That $Vintage Cow Bell$ at the Museum really took me back! Grandma had one just like it!

english: I'm kidding! Gya ha ha!
french: Je plaisante ! Rah ha ha !
russian: Шучу! Га-ха-ха!

russian: Скоро уж и снегопад начнётся. Будем греться дома у огня!
bulgarian: Soon enough the snow will start falling and we'll be getting cozy by the fire!

english: Starting to get chilly when the sun goes down.
french: Il commence à faire frisquet, quand le soleil se couche.
russian: После захода уже слегка подмораживает.
bulgarian: Starting to get chilly when the sun goes down.

english: I wish they could understand that I won't let them go hungry!
french: Si seulement ils comprenaient que je ne les laisserai jamais avoir faim !
russian: Вот бы они знали, что я их голодными не оставлю!
bulgarian: I wish they could understand that I won't let them go hungry!

english: The animals must know winter is on the way, they're really putting away the feed.
french: Mes animaux savent que l'hiver arrive et ils mettent plein de nourriture de côté.
russian: Мои животные чуют, что зима на носу. Откладывают корм на будущее.
bulgarian: The animals must know winter is on the way, they're really putting away the feed.

english: Feels like nature is putting on a show just for us!
french: Ça me donne l'impression que la nature nous offre un spectacle rien que pour nous !
russian: Кажется, будто природа решила для нас принарядиться!
bulgarian: Feels like nature is putting on a show just for us!

english: Isn't fall wonderful?
french: C'est merveilleux, l'automne, non ?
russian: Осень — такая чудесная пора!
bulgarian: Isn't fall wonderful?

english: It looks like it's going to be another great day!
french: La journée s'annonce encore fantastique !
russian: Вижу, нас ждёт ещё один прекрасный день!
bulgarian: It looks like it's going to be another great day!

english: Good morning, [Ari].
french: Bonjour, [Ari].
russian: Доброе утро, [Ari].
bulgarian: Good morning, [Ari].

english: Hope you slept as well as I did last night.
french: J'espère que tu as dormi aussi bien que moi, cette nuit.
russian: Надеюсь, тебе ночью спалось не хуже, чем мне.
bulgarian: Hope you slept as well as I did last night.

english: Morning!
french: Bonjour !
russian: Утречка!
bulgarian: Morning!

english: I'm sure you're not doing any better. Come on, let's help each other dry off.
french: Je suis sûr que ça n'est pas mieux pour toi. Viens, on va se sécher mutuellement.
russian: Да и тебе наверняка не легче. Пойдём, поможем друг другу обсохнуть.
bulgarian: I'm sure you're not doing any better. Come on, let's help each other dry off.

english: Whew, I'm soaked through from this rain!
french: Pfiou, je suis trempé jusqu'aux os, avec cette pluie !
russian: Фух, я в этом дожде вымок насквозь!
bulgarian: Whew, I'm soaked through from this rain!

english: It really is a farmer's friend, isn't it? Feels like my whole schedule just opened up!
french: La pluie est vraiment l'amie du fermier, hein ? C'est comme si mon planning venait de s'alléger d'un coup !
russian: Это фермеру подмога, верно? У меня сразу так много свободного времени появилось!
bulgarian: It really is a farmer's friend, isn't it? Feels like my whole schedule just opened up!

english: Rainy today...
french: Une journée pluvieuse...
russian: Дождливый денёк...
bulgarian: Rainy today...

english: Well, no harm in taking it a little easier today!
french: Bah, ce n'est pas grave si j'y vais tranquillement, aujourd'hui !
russian: Что ж, не беда, сегодня буду работать полегче!
bulgarian: Well, no harm in taking it a little easier today!

english: Phew, hardly feel rested at all for some reason.
french: Pfiou, je ne sais pas pourquoi, mais je ne me sens pas reposé du tout.
russian: Фух, я почему-то будто и совсем не спал.
bulgarian: Phew, hardly feel rested at all for some reason.

english: We'd best settle in for the night.
french: On ferait aussi bien de se préparer à aller se coucher.
russian: Давай побудем дома до утра.
bulgarian: We'd best settle in for the night.

english: Looks like it's only snowing harder...
french: On dirait qu'il neige de plus en plus fort...
russian: Кажется, снегопад только усиливается...
bulgarian: Looks like it's only snowing harder...

english: Nothing to do but get ourselves fired up to go out and brave the day!
french: Bon, il ne nous reste qu'à nous motiver pour affronter cette journée !
russian: Ничего не поделать — придётся собраться с духом и бросить вызов непогоде!
bulgarian: Nothing to do but get ourselves fired up to go out and brave the day!

english: Gya ha ha!
french: Gah ha ha !
russian: Га-ха-ха!
bulgarian: Gya ha ha!

english: Brr, would you look at that snow.
french: Brrr, regarde-moi un peu toute cette neige.
russian: Брр, ну и снегопад!
bulgarian: Brr, would you look at that snow.

english: Should be fun!
french: Et je vais passer un bon moment !
russian: Занимательное занятие!
bulgarian: Should be fun!

english: Today seems like a good day to put the livestock through their paces.
french: Ça m'a l'air d'être une bonne journée pour aller voir ce que donnent les animaux.
russian: Думаю, сегодня хороший день, чтобы испытать аллюр у скота.
bulgarian: Today seems like a good day to put the livestock through their paces.

english: There's just too much to do in spring, no use being hard on myself.
french: Il y a trop à faire, au printemps, inutile d'être trop dur envers moi-même.
russian: Но себя корить ни к чему: весной всегда работы много.
bulgarian: There's just too much to do in spring, no use being hard on myself.

english: I had a list as long as my arm to do today and hardly got any of it done!
french: J'avais une liste longue comme le bras de choses à faire, aujourd'hui, et je n'ai avancé sur presque rien !
russian: У меня на сегодня был список дел до пола, а я и половины не успел!
bulgarian: I had a list as long as my arm to do today and hardly got any of it done!

english: Especially when I know I'll be spending the evening with you!
french: Surtout quand je sais que je vais passer la soirée avec toi !
russian: Особенно когда я знаю, что вечер проведу с тобой!
bulgarian: Especially when I know I'll be spending the evening with you!

english: There's not much better than a spring day, is there?
french: Il n'y a rien de mieux qu'une journée de printemps, tu ne trouves pas ?
russian: Весенние деньки просто замечательные!
bulgarian: There's not much better than a spring day, is there?

english: I gotta make sure to tire'em out or they'll get up to no end of mischief.
french: Je dois faire en sorte qu'ils se dépensent beaucoup, sinon ils vont faire bêtise sur bêtise.
russian: Мне надо как следует их умаять, не то они будут бедокурить.
bulgarian: I gotta make sure to tire'em out or they'll get up to no end of mischief.

english: Spring weather's got the animals extra rambunctious.
french: Avec cette météo de printemps, les animaux sont plus agités que d'habitude.
russian: От весенней погоды животные так раззадорились.
bulgarian: Spring weather's got the animals extra rambunctious.

english: It makes doing a supply run into town a breeze!
french: Aller se réapprovisionner en ville devient une promenade de santé !
russian: Даже за продуктами в город несёшься окрылённый!
bulgarian: It makes doing a supply run into town a breeze!

english: Everyone's in such a good mood in the spring.
french: Tout le monde est de tellement bonne humeur, au printemps.
russian: Весной у всех такое хорошее настроение.
bulgarian: Everyone's in such a good mood in the spring.

english: Least now that I'm at home I can finally walk around in my underwear.
french: Enfin, maintenant que je suis à la maison, je peux au moins me balader en sous-vêtements.
russian: Зато теперь я хотя бы дома, так что могу ходить в белье.
bulgarian: Least now that I'm at home I can finally walk around in my underwear.

english: I've been sweating all day and this heat ain't letting up!
french: J'ai passé la journée à transpirer et la chaleur ne baisse pas !
russian: Я весь день потею, а жара и не думает заканчиваться!
bulgarian: I've been sweating all day and this heat ain't letting up!

english: You can tell they appreciate the cooler temperatures too.
french: Il est évident qu'elles aussi apprécient des températures plus fraîches.
russian: Сразу видно: они тоже любители прохладны.
bulgarian: You can tell they appreciate the cooler temperatures too.

english: Days cooling off, and listen to those cicadas!
french: Les températures redescendent enfin et écoute un peu ces cigales !
russian: Жара постепенно отходит. Послушай, как стрекочут цикады!
bulgarian: Days cooling off, and listen to those cicadas!

english: Still, nothing that an extra large cup of coffee won't fix.
french: Mais bon, rien qu'une très grande tasse de café ne saurait régler.
russian: Ни ничего, двойная порция кофе выручает, как всегда.
bulgarian: Still, nothing that an extra large cup of coffee won't fix.

english: Hard to get a good night's sleep in this heat, ain't it?
french: Difficile de bien dormir la nuit avec cette chaleur, hein ?
russian: В такую жару даже выспаться как следует трудно.
bulgarian: Hard to get a good night's sleep in this heat, ain't it?

english: Let's make the most of 'em!
french: Profitons-en au maximum !
russian: Давай проведём их с пользой!
bulgarian: Let's make the most of 'em!

english: These hot summer days make me feel like a kid again.
french: Pendant ces chaudes journées d'été, j'ai l'impression d'être à nouveau un gosse.
russian: В эти жаркие летние деньки я снова чувствую себя мальчишкой.
bulgarian: These hot summer days make me feel like a kid again.

english: I gotta talk to Louis about it. He'll be able to come up with something.
french: Il faut que j'en parle à Louis. Il trouvera sûrement une solution.
russian: Надо обсудить это с Луи. Он обязательно что-нибудь придумает.
bulgarian: I gotta talk to Louis about it. He'll be able to come up with something.

english: Seems I can't keep the snow out of my boots this year.
french: Impossible de ne pas me retrouver avec de la neige plein les bottes, cette année.
russian: В этом году у меня никак не получается не накидать снега в ботинки.
bulgarian: Seems I can't keep the snow out of my boots this year.

english: I'll stoke the fire and you get yourself settled in!
french: Je vais alimenter le feu et toi, tu t'installes confortablement !
russian: Я подбавлю огня, а ты устраивайся поудобнее!
bulgarian: I'll stoke the fire and you get yourself settled in!

english: Nothing cozier than a winter evening.
french: Rien de plus douillet qu'une soirée d'hiver.
russian: Зимние вечера невероятно уютные.
bulgarian: Nothing cozier than a winter evening.

english: Maybe I could set up some more toys for them to play with, you know, to entice 'em.
french: Je devrais peut-être mettre en place de nouveaux jouets, pour qu'ils s'amusent, pour les appâter.
russian: Может, поставить им во дворе больше игрушек. Ну, знаешь, привлечь внимание.
bulgarian: Maybe I could set up some more toys for them to play with, you know, to entice 'em.

english: Even when the weather is clear, if it's too cold the animals need to be coaxed out.
french: Même si le ciel est dégagé, s'il fait trop froid, les animaux ont besoin d'être cajolés pour accepter de sortir.
russian: Даже когда на дворе ясно, в холода животных приходится выманивать.
bulgarian: Even when the weather is clear, if it's too cold the animals need to be coaxed out.

english: And it's even better with you by my side.
french: Et c'est encore mieux avec toi à mes côtés.
russian: А с тобой под боком — ещё лучше.
bulgarian: And it's even better with you by my side.

english: I always sleep the best in winter, nice and cozy under thick blankets.
french: C'est toujours en hiver que je dors le mieux, confortablement installé sous d'épaisses couvertures.
russian: Мне лучше всего спится зимой, в тепле и уюте под толстым одеялом.
bulgarian: I always sleep the best in winter, nice and cozy under thick blankets.

english: I think it'll be a real treat for the animals!
french: Ce sera un vrai cadeau pour les animaux !
russian: Думаю, получится отменное лакомство!
bulgarian: I think it'll be a real treat for the animals!

english: Working on a plan for a new feed formula.
french: Je travaille pour mettre au point une nouvelle formule d'alimentation.
russian: Я разрабатываю новую кормовую смесь для животных.
bulgarian: Working on a plan for a new feed formula.

english: I'm glad you got me into it, I've really been enjoying it!
french: Je suis content que tu m'aies incité à le faire, j'aime vraiment beaucoup ça !
russian: Это оказалось действительно интересное занятие, так что спасибо за совет!
bulgarian: I'm glad you got me into it, I've really been enjoying it!

english: Don't mind me, just taking a little time to journal.
french: Ne t'occupe pas de moi, je prends juste un peu de temps pour consigner des choses dans mon journal.
russian: Не обращай внимания, я тут просто веду дневник потихоньку.
bulgarian: Don't mind me, just taking a little time to journal.

english: It's nice to look back at the logs and see what my ancestors were up to.
french: C'est agréable de regarder les carnets de bord et de voir ce que faisaient mes ancêtres.
russian: Приятно, когда можно открыть записи и посмотреть, чем занимались твои предки.
bulgarian: It's nice to look back at the logs and see what my ancestors were up to.

english: They had a lot of smart ideas!
french: Ils avaient plein d'idées ingénieuses !
russian: У них было много находчивых идей!
bulgarian: They had a lot of smart ideas!

english: Sweetwater Farm has been in the family for hundreds of years.
french: La ferme de Doucerive est dans ma famille depuis des centaines d'années.
russian: Ферма «Сладководье» сотни лет передаётся по наследству.
bulgarian: Sweetwater Farm has been in the family for hundreds of years.

english: Would you look at those coat colors!
french: Regarde un peu toutes ces couleurs de pelage !
russian: Погляди, какие шикарные окрасы!
bulgarian: Would you look at those coat colors!

english: Livestock Living's newest issue is out.
french: Le dernier numéro de « La revue du bétail » est sorti.
russian: Пришёл новый выпуск «Скотоводства и Жизни».
bulgarian: Livestock Living's newest issue is out.

english: You know, [Ari], there's plenty of room for two!
french: Tu sais, [Ari], il y a largement la place pour deux !
russian: Знаешь, [Ari], тут ведь и на двоих хватит места!
bulgarian: You know, [Ari], there's plenty of room for two!

english: Nothing like taking a load off after a busy day!
french: Rien de tel que de se poser après une journée bien occupée !
russian: Как хорошо раскинуться и отдохнуть после рабочего дня!
bulgarian: Nothing like taking a load off after a busy day!

english: I thought it'd be a light read, but the mystery is actually getting intense...
french: Je croyais que ce serait une lecture pas compliquée, mais l'intrigue commence à être prenante...
russian: Я ожидал лёгкое чтиво, но тут так драматично закручивается сюжет...
bulgarian: I thought it'd be a light read, but the mystery is actually getting intense...

english: This book is about a talking cow that solves mysteries!
french: Ce livre raconte l'histoire d'une vache parlante qui résout des énigmes !
russian: Это книга про говорящую корову-детектива!
bulgarian: This book is about a talking cow that solves mysteries!

english: After all, quality crops are the first step to raising prize winning animals!
french: Après tout, des cultures de qualité sont le premier pas pour élever des animaux capables de remporter des prix !
russian: Ведь качественная кормовая база — первый шаг к победе в конкурсах животных!
bulgarian: After all, quality crops are the first step to raising prize winning animals!

english: Thought I'd try my hand at growing some new varieties, see how they do.
french: Je me suis dit que j'allais essayer de faire pousser de nouvelles variétés, pour voir ce que ça donne.
russian: Я решил попробовать разводить другие сорта. Посмотрю, что из этого выйдет.
bulgarian: Thought I'd try my hand at growing some new varieties, see how they do.

english: Thought I'd do a little experimenting to see if I can figure out how that's happening!
french: Je me suis dit que j'allais faire quelques tests pour tenter de comprendre comment ça se produit !
russian: Я решил поэкспериментировать и выяснить, в чём тут дело!
bulgarian: Thought I'd do a little experimenting to see if I can figure out how that's happening!

english: Sometimes I'll end up with a particular crop that's just tastier than the rest.
french: Il arrive parfois qu'une de mes cultures en particulier se révèle plus savoureuse que les autres.
russian: Иногда бывает, что с одного куста плоды вкуснее всех остальных.
bulgarian: Sometimes I'll end up with a particular crop that's just tastier than the rest.

english: So I thought I'd see if I could find a way to make the plants up their yield!
french: Je me suis donc dit que j'allais essayer de trouver le moyen d'améliorer le rendement de mes cultures !
russian: Так что я решил попробовать увеличить урожайность растений!
bulgarian: So I thought I'd see if I could find a way to make the plants up their yield!

english: Fall crops are already plenty bountiful, but Sweetwater Farm doesn't have a lot of land for fields.
french: Les récoltes d'automne sont déjà généreuses, mais à la ferme de Doucerive, il n'y a pas beaucoup de terrain pour les champs.
russian: Осенние культуры и так очень плодородны, но на ферме «Сладководье» не очень много пахотной земли.
bulgarian: Fall crops are already plenty bountiful, but Sweetwater Farm doesn't have a lot of land for fields.

english: I'd like to see if I can grow something that's even better at resisting the cold.
french: J'aimerais voir si j'arrive à faire pousser quelque chose qui soit capable de résister encore mieux au froid.
russian: Я хочу попробовать вырастить что-нибудь ещё более морозостойкое.
bulgarian: I'd like to see if I can grow something that's even better at resisting the cold.

english: Winters here are pretty mild, but...
french: Les hivers sont assez doux, ici, mais...
russian: Зимы здесь довольно мягкие, но всё же...
bulgarian: Winters here are pretty mild, but...

english: No matter how things shake out, I'd say we have a good chance of bringing that blue ribbon home!
bulgarian: No matter how things shake out, I'd say we have a good chance of bringing that blue ribbon home!

english: Good morning, [Ari]! Are you ready for the $Animal Festival$?
bulgarian: Good morning, [Ari]! Are you ready for the $Animal Festival$?

english: I'm looking forward to cutting a rug with you!
bulgarian: I'm looking forward to cutting a rug with you!

english: Morning, [Ari]! It's the $Harvest Festival$ today!
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! It's the $Harvest Festival$ today!

english: Don't suppose you'd want to sneak out to the Summit with me tonight, would you?
bulgarian: Don't suppose you'd want to sneak out to the Summit with me tonight, would you?

english: Morning, [Ari]! It's the $Shooting Star Festival$ today, isn't it?
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! It's the $Shooting Star Festival$ today, isn't it?

english: I'm really looking forward to seeing all the flowers this year!
bulgarian: I'm really looking forward to seeing all the flowers this year!

english: I spent the whole morning thinking about the $Spring Festival$...
bulgarian: I spent the whole morning thinking about the $Spring Festival$...

english: I hear Darcy's got some new teas in... I might have myself some of that!
bulgarian: I hear Darcy's got some new teas in... I might have myself some of that!

english: Morning, [Ari]! It's Market day!
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! It's Market day!

english: I need a new belt, and I can catch up with him besides.
bulgarian: I need a new belt, and I can catch up with him besides.

english: Market day's here! I might stop by Louis'.
bulgarian: Market day's here! I might stop by Louis'.

english: Thinking I might see what Merri's got in. I like when she stocks the rustic looking stuff.
bulgarian: Thinking I might see what Merri's got in. I like when she stocks the rustic looking stuff.

english: Morning, [Ari]! It's Market day!
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! It's Market day!

english: Stillwell sent me a letter saying terrible things will happen unless we change the future...
bulgarian: Stillwell sent me a letter saying terrible things will happen unless we change the future...

english: I don't know whether it's true or not, but I'm always happy to help that soggy little fella out!
bulgarian: I don't know whether it's true or not, but I'm always happy to help that soggy little fella out!

english: Hope you're excited for the Saturday Market today!
bulgarian: Hope you're excited for the Saturday Market today!

english: He wanted some fresh ingredients for his $Cooking Challenge$.
bulgarian: He wanted some fresh ingredients for his $Cooking Challenge$.

english: Morning, [Ari]! I've got to stop by Taliferro's booth at the Market today.
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! I've got to stop by Taliferro's booth at the Market today.

english: I'm starting to look too wild...
bulgarian: I'm starting to look too wild...

english: I only need to look a little wild.
bulgarian: I only need to look a little wild.

english: It's Market day, and I'm thinking about stopping by Vera's for a haircut...
bulgarian: It's Market day, and I'm thinking about stopping by Vera's for a haircut...

english: Wheedle said he's got some big livestock secrets for me, at a reasonable price!
bulgarian: Wheedle said he's got some big livestock secrets for me, at a reasonable price!

english: I've got to check it out!
bulgarian: I've got to check it out!

english: Morning, [Ari]! Happy Saturday!
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! Happy Saturday!

english: I want to stop by Zorel's booth today and pick up some new music...
bulgarian: I want to stop by Zorel's booth today and pick up some new music...

english: Something we can dance to in the kitchen, you know?
bulgarian: Something we can dance to in the kitchen, you know?

english: It's Market day, [Ari]!
bulgarian: It's Market day, [Ari]!

english: Feels like I'm walking on air.
french: J'ai l'impression de marcher sur un petit nuage.
russian: Я сейчас будто витаю в облаках.
bulgarian: Feels like I'm walking on air.

english: The wedding, the party... the whole town coming out to celebrate with us...
french: Le mariage, la fête... Toute la ville qui vient se réjouir avec nous...
russian: Свадьба, потом праздник... Все горожане пришли нас поздравить...
bulgarian: The wedding, the party... the whole town coming out to celebrate with us...

english: And then waking up with you by my side...
french: Et ensuite, me réveiller avec toi à mes côtés...
russian: А потом я проснулся с тобой под боком...
bulgarian: And then waking up with you by my side...

english: I couldn't be happier.
french: Je ne pourrais pas être plus heureux.
russian: Я счастливее всех на свете.
bulgarian: I couldn't be happier.

english: I love you, Hayden!
french: Je t'aime, Hayden !
russian: Я люблю тебя, Хейден.
bulgarian: I love you, Hayden!
